candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether contractor availability, claim frequency/severity, renewal rates, and service cost inflation are improving or worsening as housing turnover remains constrained.

candidates.node_relation: Direct exposure to home warranty, repair dispatch, independent contractor networks, and on-demand home repair services.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Home warranty and home repair services
candidates.theme_relation: Second-order consumer housing beneficiary if homeowners repair, maintain, and insure existing homes instead of transacting or moving.
candidates.why_include: Frontdoor is unusually close to the node: its American Home Shield and 2-10 Home Buyers Warranty brands sit between homeowners, builders, insurers, appliances/systems, and local contractors. The bottleneck angle is not product scarcity but dispatch density, service-provider availability, claims workflow, and repair fulfillment quality.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Housing discussions often focus on mortgage rates, homebuilders, big-box retail, and brokers. A home-warranty/repair-network company can be misclassified as generic consumer services rather than as a repair-capacity and dispatch rail.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether ServiceTitan can keep expanding beyond core residential trades into commercial, roofing, and larger enterprise contractors without cyclicality overwhelming software adoption.
candidates.next_evidence: Review FY2026 10-K, customer cohort metrics, net revenue retention if disclosed, large-contractor penetration, payments/fintech attach rate, and churn sensitivity during weaker repair/remodel cycles.
candidates.node_relation: Provides cloud-based workflow software for contractors, including back-office, customer-experience, and trade-business operations.
candidates.theme_relation: A software rail for fragmented local repair capacity; benefits if HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing, and commercial/residential service contractors digitize dispatch, estimating, invoicing, and customer management.
candidates.why_include: The chokepoint hypothesis emphasizes fragmented local service capacity. ServiceTitan is a public-market way to map that capacity through the software layer rather than owning trucks or technicians.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Despite being newly public and software-covered, it is less obvious in a consumer/housing funnel because it screens as vertical SaaS, not housing repair infrastructure.

candidates.why_include: AppFolio maps the rental-operations rail: leasing, maintenance coordination, resident/owner workflows, payments, screening, and property-manager productivity.
candidates.why_underfollowed: It is often categorized as application software or real-estate tech, so its link to consumer housing stress, rental operations, and local maintenance workflows may be missed in a discretionary/consumer screen.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether title order volumes, commercial revenue, refinance recovery, and information-services growth are improving enough to offset cyclicality and regulatory pressure.

candidates.node_relation: Regulated title, escrow, settlement-risk, property-data, valuation, mortgage-subservicing, and home-warranty-adjacent services.

candidates.why_underfollowed: Not deeply underfollowed, so it belongs in the reference lane. The useful insight is not obscurity but its role as a benchmark for regulated transaction infrastructure and title-data moats.

memory_update.text: FTDR should remain a core underfollowed candidate for the housing repair/warranty dispatch rail; verify contractor-network quality, claims inflation, renewal rates, and member growth.
TTAN maps fragmented contractor capacity through software rather than labor ownership; useful for a scarce workflow/dispatch rail, but watch valuation, churn, and housing-service cyclicality.
APPF is a rental-operations workflow rail with measurable units under management; include in later layers if evidence supports durable value-added services and low regulatory risk.

For this node, the likely chokepoints are contractor network density, embedded property-management workflows, regulated title/escrow processes, title/property data assets, and repair/warranty claims-routing infrastructure rather than physical materials.

Need a later focused pass on smaller speculative names and adjacent private/public comparables in home inspection software, move/utility concierge, property-maintenance marketplaces, and title-production software; PRCH is a candidate but not yet core due to insurance complexity.

node: Housing repair, rental operations, property services, title/escrow, warranty, and dispatch rails
summary: Expanded the node toward scarce service rails rather than homebuilders: contractor dispatch/workflow software, home-warranty repair networks, property-management operating systems, and regulated title/escrow/data infrastructure. The underfollowed lane is strongest where local contractor capacity, embedded workflow data, or compliance-heavy transaction processes create switching costs. Current pass is research-only and does not imply any trading recommendation.
